diagram_math_checks.justification: Definition lines 40–46 permits any finite simple oriented graph and D subset V. Chosen V=(v1,v2,v3), E=(e1,e2) is a simple path; I={v1,v2}, D={v3}. Two drawn edges give degrees (1,2,1). All three vertices and two directed segments occur in the native SVG and original-resolution preview. No closing edge is asserted or required.

Definition lines 42–44 and the local incidence supplier assign -1 at the tail and +1 at the head. e1:v1 to v2 gives (-1,1,0)^T and e2:v2 to v3 gives (0,-1,1)^T; these are exactly the displayed 3 by 2 matrix B. Arrows encode orientation only, as explicitly stated in the caption.
With C=diag(c1,c2), BCB^T=c1(-1,1,0)^T(-1,1,0)+c2(0,-1,1)^T(0,-1,1), yielding precisely the displayed symmetric 3 by 3 L_C. Labels do not strengthen c_e>=0; zero conductances remain allowed.

Definition lines 46–52 gives M=diag(m1,m2), m1,m2>0, and L_D=(L_C)_{I,I}. Deleting row/column 3 leaves [[c1,-c1],[-c1,c1+c2]], agreeing with the figure and displayed 2 by 2 matrices. Grounding v3 does not delete c2 from entry (2,2).

This definition has no proof section. The diagram illustrates a special case only; the original definition remains byte-identical and the displayed calculations follow algebraically from it without appeal to the figure.
